walkthrough: Goal: soften something already painted with a Gaussian blur or crisp it with Sharpen, see the change on the canvas while setting it, keep it or drop it, limit it to a selection, take it back and find it again after reopening.

Entry: on an empty library (2880 x 1800, landscape) widen the brush with the side bar's size slider and paint a few black lines on Layer 1 with the Ink Pen. In the left island the wand (Adjustments) opens the popover headed Adjustments with four rows: Hue, Saturation, Brightness; Curves; Gaussian Blur; Sharpen (Procreate's order).

Gaussian Blur: tapping the row closes the menu; a panel grows from the wand (it keeps the ink ring) headed Gaussian Blur with one slider, Radius, at 0 % (no change), then Reset (grey), Cancel and Apply. Pressing the slider and sliding right blurs the lines as the hand moves: at 100 % the blur's standard deviation is 32 canvas pixels (1 % is about a third of a pixel); the lines' edges fade into the paper without darkening it. The fingers still move the view; the pen draws nothing while the panel shows.

Apply keeps the blur as it shows, as one step: the panel goes back into the wand; one undo gives the sharp lines back, redo the blurred ones. Tapping the wand while adjusting applies too, and so does choosing any other tool or edit.

Sharpen: the row opens the panel headed Sharpen with one slider, Amount, at 0 %. Sliding it right makes each line's edge crisper (unsharp masking over 1 canvas pixel: 100 % adds twice the difference from that blur). Cancel drops it: the panel goes and the canvas is as it was. Sharpen again, Amount up, Apply keeps it.

Selection: with a rectangle selected over the lines' left half, Gaussian Blur at a larger radius blurs only inside the rectangle, its edge hard, reading the paint just outside; the selection stays after Apply.
Zoom and export: a blur is evaluated at canvas resolution and enlarged smoothly in the sharp-zoom tiers and in 2x and 4x exports; strokes drawn after it stay sharp.
Reopen after the system closed the app: every applied blur and sharpen shows as it was applied.
Not here: Motion and Perspective Blur, Procreate's Pencil mode (filtering by painting), blur respecting Alpha Lock.
